proposal_text: This research proposes to develop a machine learning model to optimise hospital bed allocation across three Dublin hospitals. The model will predict patient length of stay, readmission risk, and discharge timing using electronic health records including diagnosis codes, vital signs, medication history, and demographic information including age, gender, and medical card status. The training dataset consists of 80,000 anonymised patient records from 2018-2024. The model will generate daily recommendations for bed managers on patient transfers and early discharge candidates. The researchers acknowledge that medical card status (a proxy for socioeconomic deprivation) could influence the model's predictions in ways that disadvantage lower-income patients. The model outputs will be advisory but will be integrated into the hospital's electronic patient record system. No mechanism for clinical override documentation has been designed.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Psychological Harm

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Discrimination

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Data Governance

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Dignity
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of degrading, objectifying, or otherwise undermining human dignity through AI system design or use.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Financial Harm

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Reputational Harm

retrieved_risk_categories.label: False Identification
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk of incorrect identity attribution (e.g. facial-recognition false matches) with consequential harm.

retrieved_risk_categories.label: Transparency
retrieved_risk_categories.definition: Risk that an AI system's operation, capabilities, limitations, or decision rationale are not adequately disclosed to end-users and stakeholders.

assessment.risk_summary: The proposed research project involves developing a machine learning model to optimise hospital bed allocation, which poses risks related to discrimination, privacy breach, and psychological harm. The model's use of medical card status as a proxy for socioeconomic deprivation may disadvantage lower-income patients, and the lack of a mechanism for clinical override documentation raises concerns about accountability. The project also involves processing sensitive personal data, including electronic health records, which increases the risk of data breaches and privacy violations.
